result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_preferential_attachment_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a bipartite graph grown by preferential attachment on its second part. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_preferential_attachment_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a bipartite graph grown by preferential attachment on its second part. title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_preferential_attachment_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a bipartite graph grown by preferential attachment on its second part. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a bipartite graph grown by preferential attachment on its second part. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14041-L14152){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_bipartite_preferential_attachment_graph( aseq, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, part_attr="part", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bipartite preferential attachment graph](../assets/graphs/add-bipartite-preferential-attachment-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three bipartite preferential attachment graphs in which three accent top nodes bring two edges each, and each edge makes a new teal bottom node with probability p or else picks an existing one in proportion to its degree. At p=1 every edge gets its own node, six in all; at p=0.5 the six edges share three bottom nodes, the busiest taking three; and at p=0 every edge lands on the single node the first edge made, so each top node reaches it twice, drawn as bowed pairs." width="100%"} Creates `len(aseq)` nodes in a first part, then grows a second part while wiring them: first-part node `i` gets exactly `aseq[i]` edges, handed out node by node. Each edge goes, with probability `p`, to a brand-new second-part node, and otherwise to an existing second-part node chosen with probability proportional to its current degree (the first edge always creates a node). Popular second-part nodes therefore keep getting more popular, and their degrees end up heavy-tailed, while the number of second-part nodes is random, about `p` times the number of edges. The same pair can be joined twice, so the graph can have parallel edges. The process is NetworkX's `bipartite.preferential_attachment_graph()`. Each node's part is stored in the `part_attr=` node attribute (`0` for the first, `1` for the second). Second-part nodes are created in the order they first get an edge, after all the first-part nodes, and in a directed graph every edge points from the first part to the second. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Bipartite preferential attachment graphs are useful for: - modeling two-mode networks where one side's popularity snowballs, such as users and the hashtags, tags or products they pick - collaboration-style data (authors and papers, actors and films) with a few very popular items - testing bipartite measures on heavy-tailed degree distributions ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [aseq]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges of each first-part node, as a list of non-negative integers. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability, between `0` and `1`, that an edge creates a new second-part node rather than attaching to an existing one. With `p=1` every edge gets its own node; with `p=0` all edges go to the single node the first edge created. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [part_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["part"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's part (`0` or `1`). Default is `"part"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an entry of `aseq=` is negative or `p=` is outside `0` to `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fifty first-part nodes with three edges each. About `p = 0.3` of the 150 edges open a new second-part node: ::: {#2b384c62 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_bipartite_preferential_attachment_graph([3] * 50, p=0.3, seed=2) parts = graph.get_node_df()["part"] (parts == 0).sum(), (parts == 1).sum(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 41, 150) ``` ::: ::: The second part's degrees are heavy-tailed: most nodes have one or two edges, and a few early ones collect many: ::: {#4a125408 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = graph.get_node_df() sorted(df.filter(df["part"] == 1)["degree"].to_list(), reverse=True)[:8] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [56, 11, 8, 7, 6, 4, 4, 4] ``` ::: :::
